headline: Nvidia beats and guides above estimates after a broad selloff drove the S&P 500 down 1.0%
subhead: The S&P 500 fell 1.0 percent to 7,340.5 with all 11 sectors lower and Salesforce down 9.4 percent; Nvidia then reported 115.8 billion dollars in revenue and guided to 130 billion.

us.text: S&P 500 fell 1.0 percent to 7,340.5, Dow 1.6 percent and Nasdaq 0.7 percent, a fourth straight loss, with every sector lower before Nvidia results.
Nvidia posted about 115.8 billion dollars in quarterly revenue and guided to 130 billion versus 125.25 billion expected; shares rose nearly 4 percent after hours.
Software sank on AI disruption fears before Anthropic prices its IPO: Salesforce fell 9.4 percent and Intuit 7.2 percent; futures price a 95.4 percent chance of a December Fed hike.

india.text: On Tuesday the Nifty rose 96.3 points to 25,387.4 and Sensex 427.4 points to 82,532.2, as Bank Nifty hit a record; the price feed here still shows Monday.
FIIs net bought about 4,195 crore rupees in cash on Tuesday and DIIs about 197 crore, extending the foreign buying streak.
Rupee firmed to 93.46 per dollar, up 0.5 percent, on lower Brent crude and foreign fund inflows.

global.text: Taiwan fell 6.0 percent on Monday as TSMC led an AI chip rout; Nikkei and Hang Seng fell on Tuesday as new US chip curbs hit tech.
STOXX 600 dropped 1.75 percent to 650.72, its worst day since March, as European tech lost 3.9 percent; SAP's ADR fell 4.8 percent.
Dollar index held near a 19-month high on Fed hike bets; gold stayed near one-year lows at about 3,850 dollars while Brent settled at 93.14.

weekly.narrative: Jensen Huang's sudden exit as Nvidia CEO dominated the week: Nvidia fell 12.8 percent, but rotation into Apple, AMD and Broadcom still left the S&P 500 up 2.5 percent and the Nasdaq up 2.3 percent despite a Friday AI selloff. Hot US CPI and 6.5 percent annual PPI pushed the 10-year yield to 5.15 percent and left a December Fed hike fully priced, lifting the dollar to a 19-month high. That weighed on metals and crypto: gold fell 4.5 percent to a 13-month low, silver 6.1 percent and bitcoin broke below 70,000 dollars. India leaned on nine straight sessions of foreign buying and a bank rally, though the Nifty slipped to 25,144.3 on Friday after October CPI rose to 6.09 percent. Next week brings Nvidia results on 17 November, FOMC minutes on 18 November and Anthropic's expected Nasdaq debut on 19 November.
